answer: Grades are sealed when submitted and only opened at close, so graders cannot react to or copy each other, which prevents a Sybil cluster from coordinating its votes within a single jury. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a sable as the anchor of the cost.
